title: Unboring AI Alternatives: Face Swap Workflows and Free Limits
summary: Compare Magic Hour, Remaker, Reface/Unboring, DeepSwap and FaceFusion by templates, custom media, multi-face support, local control and accepted-output cost.
body_markdown:
Choose Magic Hour when you want to swap a face in your own photo or video in a browser; Remaker when multi-face and longer uploaded-video workflows need evaluation; Reface/Unboring when its template catalog is the point; DeepSwap for a hosted custom-media workflow; or FaceFusion when local operation and technical control justify installation. Test the same permitted source face and representative clip before paying or moving a production workflow.


These are current workflow choices, not a controlled visual-quality ranking. Product pages and repositories were checked September 13, 2026. Free allowances, watermarks, plans and upload limits change; verify the actual export before committing.


## What Unboring does


[Unboring by Reface](https://reface.ai/unboring) combines face swapping, photo animation and a catalog of photo and video templates. It is most relevant when you want to place a permitted face into a ready-made entertainment format. A template library is a different job from editing your own campaign footage or operating a model locally.


-


**Magic Hour:** **browser photo and video face-swap workflows using your own media.**


-


**Remaker:** hosted video, GIF and multi-face workflows with duration-based credit use.


-


**Reface/Unboring:** template-first entertainment and quick social edits.


-


**DeepSwap:** hosted custom photo and video face swaps.


-


**FaceFusion:** self-managed face manipulation with local installation and job controls.


## 1. Magic Hour: your own photo or video


Magic Hour’s[Face Swap](https://magichour.ai/products/face-swap) exposes separate browser workflows for photos and videos. The public page currently documents five guest photo swaps per day without a watermark and three guest video swaps per day, up to ten seconds at 480p, with a watermark. Signed-in and paid behavior differs; check[current pricing and terms](https://magichour.ai/pricing) for the intended use.


**Choose it when:** you have your own permitted source and target media and want a direct browser test. **Check first:** face count, source angle, clip length, output resolution, watermark, commercial terms and continuity through motion, turns, cuts and occlusion.


## 2. Remaker: longer and multi-face hosted workflows


Remaker’s[current video face-swap page](https://remaker.ai/video-face-swap-online/) accepts video, GIF or WebP uploads, documents single- and multi-face workflows and currently lists a 500 MB, 30-minute upload boundary with credit use per second. Provider limits and actual available modes can differ by account and destination page.


**Choose it when:** multi-face or longer uploaded clips are central to the job. **Check first:** the selected single- or multi-face mode, duration charged, face mapping across cuts, output resolution, download, privacy terms and cost per accepted clip.


## 3. Reface/Unboring: use the template catalog


Stay with[Unboring](https://reface.ai/unboring) when the available photo or video template is the deliverable. Its current page also supports user photos and videos and multiple faces, but the catalog remains the clearest reason to choose it over a source-media-first workflow.


**Choose it when:** a specific licensed or permitted template saves the creative setup. **Check first:** rights to the template and face, whether custom uploads are available, current export quality, watermark, account offer and whether the result can be used at the intended destination.


## 4. DeepSwap: another hosted custom-media option


[DeepSwap](https://www.deepswap.ai/en/) currently presents browser face swapping for video and photos. It belongs in a shortlist when you want to compare another managed service without installing a local stack.


**Choose it when:** a hosted custom-media workflow is required and you can test before committing. **Check first:** supported media, face count, duration, output, download conditions, current plan, deletion or retention terms and complete-clip continuity.


## 5. FaceFusion: self-managed technical control


[FaceFusion’s official repository](https://github.com/facefusion/facefusion) provides local installation and job controls for a self-managed face-manipulation workflow. The project warns that installation requires technical skill and documents Windows, macOS and Linux paths.


**Choose it when:** local processing, repeatable jobs or technical configuration matters more than a hosted interface. **Check first:** license, supported accelerator, dependencies, models, output resolution, processing time, maintenance, security and the operational cost of owning the stack.


## How to compare face-swap tools fairly


-


**Use one permitted test set.** Include a clear face and a representative clip with turns, expressions, occlusion, motion and at least one cut.


-


**Keep the edit fixed.** Use the same source identity, target media, clip section and output requirement.


-


**Review every frame transition.** Check eyes, teeth, hairline, skin boundaries, glasses, hands near the face and identity after cuts.


-


**Separate failure types.** Record detection failure, wrong face mapping, identity drift, blending, flicker, resolution loss and incorrect untouched regions.


-


**Measure accepted output.** Include retries, manual repair, credits or subscription cost, local compute, setup, review and export.


-


**Verify rights and claims.** A technically clean swap can still be unusable if the likeness, footage, template, endorsement or disclosure is not permitted.


For commercial creative, use the[face-swap ads consent and disclosure checklist](https://magichour.ai/blog/face-swap-for-ads) before production. It covers the rights record, truth and endorsement review, destination-specific disclosure and audit trail that a tool comparison cannot replace.


### Run a short face-swap test


Use the same permitted face and representative clip. Review every turn, occlusion and cut, then compare the accepted output, download conditions and total work.
